2026-12-12.title: Saturday after the Sunday of the Birth of John the Baptist
2026-12-12.alt: The Twenty-Five Days' Fast before Yaldo continues.
2026-12-12.verse: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
theo: Paul ends his first letter with a burst of short commands, like a spiritual rule of life: respect those who labour among you; be at peace; admonish the idle, encourage the faint-hearted, help the weak; do not repay evil for evil. “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.” Do not quench the Spirit; test everything; hold fast to what is good.

Jesus speaks with startling seriousness about sin: better to lose a hand, a foot or an eye than to be thrown into the fire. He does not mean self-mutilation, but radical decisiveness: cut off whatever leads you or a little one into sin. Then a gentle image: “Salt is good… Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.” Salt preserves and gives flavour; in the Old Testament every offering was seasoned with “the salt of the covenant”. Our fast is a season to become salt again.

Point 2 · Cut off what causes sin

altar: The Holy Qurbono is the great thanksgiving. Here we rejoice, pray and give thanks with Christ.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, we will not quench your fire. As we gather, teach us to rejoice always, pray without ceasing and give thanks in all things. Amen.
share: Paul says: give thanks in all circumstances (1 Thessalonians 5:18). What hard circumstance can I thank God in?
Jesus speaks of stumbling blocks (Mark 9:42). What stumbling block do I need to remove?
How can I be salt in my family and workplace?
pm.resp: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all things.
interc: For the Church, that she may be salt of the earth.
For children, that no one may cause them to stumble.
For the faint-hearted and the weak, that they may be encouraged.

illus: A teacher in Kottayam began a simple habit with her class: at the end of each day, every student wrote one thing they were thankful for. By the end of the year, she said, the whole atmosphere of the class had changed.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul gives the Thessalonians a list of short commands: respect those who labour among you; be at peace among yourselves; encourage the faint-hearted, help the weak, be patient with all of them. Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you (1 Thessalonians 5:12–18).

Rejoice, pray, give thanks: three practices that can transform a life. Not rejoice when things go well, but always. Not pray when in trouble, but without ceasing. Not give thanks for good things only, but in all circumstances.
Paul adds: do not quench the Spirit. Do not despise the words of prophets, but test everything; hold fast to what is good; abstain from every form of evil (1 Thessalonians 5:19–22).

In the Gospel Jesus speaks strongly: if any of you put a stumbling block before one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for you if a great millstone were hung around your neck and you were thrown into the sea (Mark 9:42). Then he says: if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off (Mark 9:43). These are images of radical seriousness about sin.

Jesus ends: salt is good. Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another (Mark 9:50). Salt gives taste and preserves from decay. A Christian gives flavour to the world and preserves it from corruption.
During this fast, let us remove one stumbling block: a bad habit, a source of temptation, an unhealthy relationship. And let us practise Paul's three words each day: rejoice, pray, give thanks. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul says: be happy, pray always, and say thank you to God. Try all three today!

sub: Every offering was seasoned with salt.

q: You shall not omit from your grain offerings the salt of the covenant with your God;
